key_insight: DrugGen-2 improves de novo molecule generation by conditioning on both disease ontology and target protein sequence, making the design process more context-aware than target-only methods.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a practical AI pipeline for drug discovery that can better prioritize candidate compounds for specific disease-target settings and support lead generation or repurposing.
method: Fine-tune GPT-2 on curated drug–disease–target triples
Apply supervised fine-tuning, then GRPO reinforcement learning
Optimize rewards for validity, novelty, diversity, and predicted binding affinity
evidence_signal: On five diabetic nephropathy-related targets, DrugGen-2 outperformed DrugGPT and DrugGen, generating more unique molecules and showing better predicted affinities, with docking hits down to -9.917 versus -8.283 for a reference drug.
watch_item: Predicted affinity and docking gains are promising but still computational, so experimental validation is needed before biological or clinical claims can be made.
paper_title: DrugGen 2: A disease-aware language model for enhancing drug discovery
